Topic: The Physics of Pi: Colliding Blocks and Digits of Pi

Target audience: University students (Physics/Math enthusiasts)

Section: section_1 — The Hook: The Pi Mystery

Lecture lines:
Two blocks collide; Pi emerges in the count. [Asset: A_1]
How do mechanical collisions encode circle geometry? [Asset: A_2]
We track collisions as digits of Pi. [Asset: A_3]
Mass ratios dictate the number of bounces. [Asset: A_4]
Discover the surprising link between math and physics. [Asset: A_5]

Planned animations:
Draw a circle on screen #FFFFFF. Label it 'Particle Collider' in #FFD700.
Flash a point traveling towards the circle's edge #FF6347.
Show the particle bouncing off with reflection vector #00CED1.
Change the bounce point color to #FF4500.
Highlight the connection between bounce and circle curvature #FFFF00.

Section: section_2 — Prerequisite: Conservation Laws in 2D

Lecture lines:
Elastic collisions conserve both energy and momentum. [Asset: B_1]
Map velocity states to a 2D plane. [Asset: B_2]
Collisions reflect off an angled mass-ratio line. [Asset: B_3]

Planned animations:
Display two mass labels M1 and M2 in #FFFFFF.
Animate momentum vectors p1 and p2 in #00FF00.
Show collision conservation with a sum vector #FF00FF.

Section: section_3 — Mapping Collisions to Circular Arcs

Lecture lines:
Large mass ratios constrain reflection paths. [Asset: C_1]
Velocity vectors trace chords on a circle. [Asset: C_2]
More mass means smoother circular arcs. [Asset: C_3]

Planned animations:
Draw two circles representing particle states #FFFFFF.
Trace the arc path between collision states in #1E90FF.
Highlight arc segment and collision angle in #FFD700.
Show the mapping from arc length to mass ratio #00CED1.
Emphasize the constant angle property with a rotation #FF4500.

Section: section_4 — The Geometric Proof: Why Pi?

Lecture lines:
The total path angle is Pi radians. [Asset: D_1]
Collisions count how many arcs fit. [Asset: D_2]
Pi emerges from the geometry of constraints. [Asset: D_3]

Planned animations:
Construct a large circle using discrete collision points #FFFFFF.
Demonstrate arc length summing to the circumference #FF6347.
Highlight the emergence of Pi from the ratio #FFFF00.
Show the discrete points forming a smooth shape #00CED1.
Final reveal of the Pi value in the center #FFD700.

Section: section_5 — Synthesis & Conclusion

Lecture lines:
Pi appears in any bounded constraint system. [Asset: E_1]
Physics is just geometry in disguise. [Asset: E_2]
Keep counting; Pi is everywhere. [Asset: E_3]

Planned animations:
Summarize key conservation points on screen #FFFFFF.
Animate a flow showing the derivation path #1E90FF.
Final transition to the Pi-collision connection #FFD700.

import numpy as np

        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)

        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom

            for j, col in enumerate(cols):

                y = 2.2 - i * 1

        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
